1.1.name: OSI reference model
1.1.scope: Trace a web request through seven OSI layers and identify the header used at each forwarding decision.

1.2.name: Networking appliances, applications, and functions
1.2.scope: Choose appliances and services for forwarding, inspection, storage, wireless access, content delivery and traffic treatment.

1.3.name: Cloud concepts and connectivity
1.3.scope: Choose a deployment and service model, then determine how a private cloud subnet reaches an enterprise network or the internet.

1.4.name: Ports, protocols, services, and traffic types
1.4.scope: Identify services from ports, distinguish transport and IP protocols, and identify the recipients of a traffic flow.

1.5.name: Transmission media and transceivers
1.5.scope: Match an application to copper, fiber or wireless media and compatible interfaces, connectors and pluggable modules.

1.6.name: Network topologies, architectures, and types
1.6.scope: Read campus and data center diagrams, identify failure boundaries, and trace north-south and east-west flows.

1.7.name: IPv4 network addressing
1.7.scope: Calculate IPv4 subnets, distinguish address types and troubleshoot host settings with CIDR and VLSM.

1.8.name: Modern networking environments and technologies
1.8.scope: Explain controller-based networks, overlays, modern access policies, infrastructure automation and IPv6 transition.

2.1.name: Routing technologies
2.1.scope: Read routing tables, select paths, and reason about translation, redundancy and routed subinterfaces.

2.2.name: Switching technologies and features
2.2.scope: Interpret switchport membership, trunk tagging, spanning tree, link aggregation and interface settings.

2.3.name: Wireless devices and technologies
2.3.scope: Select radio bands, channels, antennas, authentication and access point designs for a coverage requirement.

2.4.name: Physical installation considerations
2.4.scope: Plan closet placement, termination, airflow, environmental controls and the rack power budget.

3.1.name: Organizational processes and procedures
3.1.scope: Use diagrams, inventories, lifecycle records, change control and a known-good configuration in daily operations.

3.2.name: Network monitoring technologies
3.2.scope: Compare logs, counters, flow data, packet captures, discovery and baselines when investigating network health.

3.3.name: Disaster recovery concepts
3.3.scope: Choose recovery sites and availability measures using tolerable downtime and acceptable data loss.

3.4.name: IPv4 and IPv6 network services
3.4.scope: Trace address assignment, name resolution and time synchronization, including IPv6 service behavior.

3.5.name: Network access and management methods
3.5.scope: Choose local, remote or out-of-band management and select an appropriate tunnel and access method.

4.1.name: Basic network security concepts
4.1.scope: Relate identity, encryption, segmentation, physical controls, compliance and deception to the assets they protect.

4.2.name: Network attacks and their impact
4.2.scope: Recognize attack symptoms and distinguish impersonation, traffic disruption and social engineering.

4.3.name: Network security features and defenses
4.3.scope: Select hardening, admission controls, filtering, zones and device protections for a stated requirement.

5.1.name: Troubleshooting methodology
5.1.scope: Move from a reproducible symptom to a tested theory, verified repair and documented outcome.

5.2.name: Cabling and physical interface issues
5.2.scope: Use cable tests, power readings, port states, error counters and optical measurements to isolate physical faults.

5.3.name: Network services troubleshooting
5.3.scope: Isolate addressing, switching, routing and service configuration faults from client and infrastructure evidence.

5.4.name: Network performance troubleshooting
5.4.scope: Use latency, jitter, loss, throughput and radio observations to distinguish resource and coverage problems.

5.5.name: Troubleshooting tools and protocols
5.5.scope: Choose the diagnostic tool or protocol that will supply the missing evidence and interpret its output.

days.title: Networking foundations
days.goal: Trace a request across two LANs and explain how device roles and topology shape its path.
days.recall: Without notes, sketch the devices between a client and a remote server. Label the addresses a switch and a router each inspect.

days.title: Network media and physical installation
days.goal: Select a link for its distance and rate, plan its installation and isolate a physical fault from test evidence.
days.recall: Recall where a frame becomes a signal. Name two physical failures that could stop the next hop from receiving that frame.

days.title: IPv4 addressing and subnetting
days.goal: Calculate subnet boundaries and usable ranges by hand, allocate unequal LANs and use the results to diagnose a host.
days.recall: Recall how a host reaches a different LAN. Which setting determines whether to send the frame to a neighbor or the gateway?

days.title: Switching, VLANs and trunks
days.goal: Trace VLAN membership and tags, select an STP path and diagnose a switching fault.
days.recall: Draw the first Ethernet frame from a /26 client to an off-subnet server. Name the destination MAC, the device that makes the Layer 3 decision and a physical check if the link is down.

days.title: Routing and connectivity
days.goal: Read a routing table, predict an address translation and isolate a missing return path.
days.recall: For 10.12.5.70/26, find the network and broadcast. Explain how traffic to a different VLAN reaches its gateway and where the Ethernet header changes.

days.title: Ports, protocols and network services
days.goal: Trace transport, address leasing, name resolution and clock synchronization from client evidence.
days.recall: Trace a DNS query to an off-subnet server through a VLAN and a PAT gateway. Identify what the switch reads, how the router picks a next hop and which fields PAT can rewrite.

days.title: Wireless networking and performance
days.goal: Choose radio settings and distinguish congestion, interference, roaming and coverage faults.
days.recall: Trace a wireless client to its gateway. Which MAC address identifies the radio connection, which VLAN should supply DHCP, and how would you test DNS only after connectivity works?

days.title: Cloud networks, IPv6 and modern architectures
days.goal: Map virtual networks, overlays and access policies. Explain address configuration and IPv6 transition choices.
days.recall: Sketch the route from a private IPv4 subnet through a PAT gateway. Which forwarding, name-resolution and access decisions would still be necessary in a virtual network?

days.title: Network operations and disaster recovery
days.goal: Use documentation, change records and recovery targets to plan service restoration.
days.recall: Recall the switchport, VLAN, route, DHCP and DNS settings one client depends on. Which records would let someone rebuild and verify that path after a failure?

days.title: Monitoring, analysis and management
days.goal: Choose a management channel, correlate logs and capture evidence, and explain deviations from a baseline.
days.recall: A wireless client can reach its VLAN gateway but cannot open a site by name. Recall which DHCP option supplies the resolver, which transports DNS uses, and which route carries an off-subnet query. How would synchronized clocks, a weekday baseline and the last approved configuration change help compare evidence?

days.title: Network security and defenses
days.goal: Recognize threats from symptoms and choose controls for identity, device access and segmentation.
days.recall: Trace a guest's HTTPS request from Wi-Fi through its VLAN, routed firewall and NAT/PAT. Where are credentials checked, where is a destination allowed, and which log records the decision? Recall how DHCP, DNS and a cloud security group could each affect this path.

days.title: Troubleshooting across the network
days.goal: Work through physical, service and performance cases. Select a test, verify a repair and document the evidence.
days.recall: Walk a voice packet from a wireless client through its AP, access VLAN, gateway and WAN. Name the physical medium, subnet decision, DNS dependency and policy boundary. Which counter or trace would separate an addressing failure from a call that connects but sounds choppy?

days.title: Timed rehearsal and error analysis
days.goal: Complete a timed N10-009 practice exam and use the results to prioritize weak objectives.
days.recall: Identify two decisions you made with low confidence and the evidence that would settle them.

days.title: Targeted remediation and exam readiness
days.goal: Retry weak skills, demonstrate a practical task independently and decide what evidence supports your exam date.
days.recall: Recall a missed concept from each weak domain before checking your notes.
